features.name: Feed list and empty state
steps: No feeds on first launch
"All feeds" shows the empty state
After adding the first feed it appears in the sidebar
Each feed shows its own unread count
After deleting the last feed the empty state returns
features.expected: With no feeds an empty-state notice must be shown rather than a blank list; each feed's unread count must be computed from real unread articles; after deleting the last feed it returns to the empty state with no residual data.

features.name: Add a feed by URL
steps: Enter "Add feed"
Enter the feed URL
Request and parse the source
Display subscribable results
After confirming, the feed is created
The first batch of articles syncs into the list
An invalid URL / unparseable content shows an error and does not create an invalid subscription
features.expected: The parsed results must come from the real source (title and articles); an invalid or unparseable address must produce an error and must not create a feed; after a successful subscription the first batch of articles must appear in the list and persist.

features.name: Multi-format parsing of RSS / Atom / JSON feeds
steps: Add an RSS, an Atom, and a JSON feed respectively
Convert all three formats uniformly into the same Feed/Article model
The title, link, publication date, body, and images are consistent between the list and the reader. The official documentation explicitly supports the three feed formats. GitHub
features.expected: The three formats must normalize into the same Feed/Article structure with consistent list and reader behavior; fields such as title, link, date, body, and images must be parsed correctly rather than left empty; parse failures should give error feedback.

features.name: Feed editing and per-feed configuration
steps: Open "Edit feed"
Edit the title and tags
Configure "full articles / summary on open / thumbnail enhancement / new content notifications / skip duplicate articles", etc.
Save
Only this feed uses these settings
Preserved after leaving and re-entering
features.expected: The configuration must apply only to that feed without affecting other subscriptions; changes must persist across exit and re-entry; title or tag changes should be reflected in sync in the navigation and lists.

features.name: Feed sync and incremental updates
steps: Existing feeds and articles
Use "Sync feeds"
Fetch the latest content from the server
Only genuinely new articles are added
The local states of existing articles, such as read and saved, are not overwritten
Syncing the same content again does not insert duplicates
features.expected: Syncing may only add genuinely new articles and duplicate content must not be inserted again; the read and saved states of existing articles must not be overwritten; a failed sync keeps the existing data and gives feedback.

features.name: Duplicate-article detection policy
steps: The feed returns duplicate content with the same GUID, URL, or title
Decide whether to create a new article based on the feed's "skip duplicate articles" and unique-ID configuration
After the policy changes, subsequent syncs follow the new rules
features.expected: With duplicate skipping enabled, articles with the same GUID or URL must not be created again; the unique-ID configuration must genuinely determine the deduplication basis; after changing the policy only subsequent syncs are affected and existing articles are not deleted.

features.name: Multi-feed aggregation and unread counting
steps: Subscribe to several feeds such as Feeder News and xkcd at the same time
"All feeds" aggregates articles from every source
Each feed maintains its own unread count
After reading an article from a feed, that feed's and the global unread counts change in sync
features.expected: "All feeds" must aggregate articles from every source and distinguish their origins; the sum of per-feed unread counts must equal the global unread count; after marking as read both the per-source and global counts decrease in sync.

features.name: Read / unread lifecycle
steps: Newly synced articles are unread by default
It becomes read after opening or performing the mark
Returning changes the list style and the unread counts
After re-marking as unread it re-enters the unread set
The state is not lost after refresh/restart
features.expected: New articles are unread by default and become read after reading or manual marking with the counts updated; re-marking as unread must return them to the unread set; the state must persist and not be lost after a refresh or restart.

features.name: Mark all as read
steps: Multiple unread articles exist within a certain scope
Choose "mark all as read"
All articles are still kept; only the read state changes
The feed's unread count and the global count become 0
Other relationships such as "saved articles" are unaffected
features.expected: The operation must only change the read state and must not delete any article; the unread count for the corresponding scope must drop to zero; other relationships such as saved and tags must stay unchanged.

features.name: Automatic mark-as-read while scrolling
steps: Enable "mark as read while scrolling"
The user scrolls through the article list
Articles that passed the reading threshold automatically become read
Unviewed items stay unread
After disabling the feature, scrolling no longer changes the state
features.expected: Only articles scrolled past the reading threshold become read while unviewed ones stay unread; after disabling the feature scrolling must no longer change the state; automatic marking must update the unread counts and persist.

features.name: Saved-article lifecycle
steps: Save an article
The article appears in "Saved articles"
The original feed page still shows the saved state
Cancel the save in "Saved articles"
The original page syncs back to not-saved
When deleting a feed, handle saved content according to the actual product's data rules
features.expected: The saved state must stay consistent between the article list and "Saved articles"; canceling the save in either place updates the other in sync; saving is not copying the article and must persist across restarts.

features.name: Article search, filtering, and sorting
steps: Enter a search term from the article list
Title/body matches are returned
Combined with unread, feed, and tag filters
Then change a sort mode such as "newest first"
The results are recomputed in real time from the same article data
Clearing the query restores the list
features.expected: Search results must match the real content of the title or body; filters and sorting can be combined over the same data source; clearing the query restores the original list state, and searching must not modify article data.

features.name: Tags and feed organization
steps: Configure tags for different feeds
Organize content by tag/feed in the navigation
After changing a tag the feed and article organization views change in sync
The article's own data is not duplicated
features.expected: Tags must be reflected in the navigation as a feed-organizing dimension; after changing a tag the organization views update in sync; article data must not be duplicated across tags, and untagged feeds are unaffected.

features.name: Background sync policy
steps: Set "look for new articles every hour"
Conditions such as "on app start / Wi-Fi only / charging only" can be combined
Background refresh runs when the conditions are met
New content is written locally
The round is skipped when the conditions are not met
It continues at the next matching condition. The official documentation confirms that Feeder supports background sync. F-Droid
features.expected: Background refresh must only run when all configured conditions are met and skip rather than error otherwise; new articles must be written locally and update the unread counts; the settings must persist and remain effective after a restart.

features.name: New content notifications
steps: Enable "new content notifications" for the feed
Syncing discovers genuinely new articles
Generate a notification
Existing articles must not repeatedly notify
After disabling notifications for this feed, articles still sync but no notifications are produced. The official documentation confirms that Feeder supports notifications. GitHub
features.expected: Only genuinely new articles produce notifications and repeated syncs must not keep alerting; the notification content must correspond to the article and link back to reading; after disabling notifications, articles should still sync without producing notifications.

features.name: Offline articles and content caching
steps: Disconnect the network after a successful sync
Cached feeds/articles can still be browsed in the list and read
Uncached full articles or images show the corresponding unavailable state
After the network returns, sync again to complete the content. Offline reading is an official core feature. F-Droid
features.expected: With the network disconnected, cached articles must still be browsable and readable; uncached content must show a clear unavailable state rather than a blank; after the network returns, syncing again should complete the content without inserting duplicate articles.

features.name: Full articles, summaries, and image enhancement
steps: Enable "fetch full articles by default" for the feed
Try to fetch the full text when the feed summary is insufficient
With "generate summary on open" enabled, a summary is generated/shown during reading
"Enhance thumbnails from article metadata" changes the image source in the list
The original feed data can still be kept
features.expected: With full articles enabled the reader should show the body rather than only the summary; summary-on-open must take effect during reading; the thumbnail-enhancement toggle should change the list image source; the original feed content must not be damaged.

features.name: Reader and content opening methods
steps: Open the article
Display the HTML content in the built-in reader according to the settings
External links open via methods such as a "custom tab"
The audio enclosure can be handed to the built-in player
After enabling paginated mode, continuous scrolling switches to page-by-page reading
features.expected: The article body must render HTML correctly in the built-in reader; external links must be handled according to the configured opening method; the pagination toggle should genuinely change the reading interaction rather than only the display.

features.name: OPML import / export round trip
steps: Multiple feeds currently exist
Export OPML
Import into a new environment
Restore the feed URLs, titles, and representable grouping structure
Existing subscriptions should be merged according to the rules rather than simply creating duplicate feeds. OPML Import/Export is an explicitly official feature. GitHub
features.expected: The exported file must contain the real feed URLs and titles; after importing, the subscriptions must match the exported content without creating duplicate feeds; representable structures such as grouping should be preserved, and invalid entries should be skipped with a notice.

features.name: Saved-article import / export and display configuration
steps: Export saved articles
Import and restore the Saved collection in another environment

It keeps different semantics from OPML "feed migration"; meanwhile display settings such as theme, dynamic color, font/zoom, card style, thumbnails, max lines, and single/double column persist across restarts
features.expected: After importing saved articles they must be restored as the Saved collection and not confused with OPML subscription migration; display settings such as theme, font, card style, and row/column counts must take effect immediately and persist across restarts.
